question: A shopkeeper offers a festival deal, "Flat Rs. 150 off on every purchase above Rs. 1000." What is the effective discount percentage if a buyer purchases an item marked Rs. 1200?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Purchase value = ₹1200, which is > ₹1000, so the flat ₹150 discount is applicable.

Discount % = (Discount Amount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

Discount % = (150 ÷ 1200) × 100

Discount % = (1 ÷ 8) × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 

 Marked Price (MP) = ₹1200

 Discount = ₹150

 Off

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the item = ₹1200

Condition for discount: Purchase value > ₹1000

Flat discount amount = ₹150

**Formula Used:**

Discount Percentage = (Discount Amount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Here, the MP (₹1200) is greater than ₹1000, so the flat discount of ₹150 is valid.

⇒ Discount % = (150 ÷ 1200) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (15 ÷ 120) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 8) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article, not on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount % = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Selling Price Formula

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100.
